subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 15, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 15, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

We hope this newsletter finds you well. As we continue to work towards making AcreetionOS the go-to Linux distribution for those seeking a user-friendly and privacy-focused experience, we wanted to take a moment to highlight some recent developments in our community.

Firstly, we're excited to announce that GNU Core Utilities 9.12 has been released. This update brings various improvements and bug fixes to the coreutils package, which is a crucial component of our distribution. We've also been made aware of a security flaw in Emacs, which has been addressed by the developers. Additionally, AlmaLinux has issued security updates for several packages, including coreutils, which we've incorporated into our distribution.

In other news, we've been working on enhancing our AI integration within AcreetionOS. Our latest commit adds context to the AI model, allowing it to better understand the nuances of our distribution and provide more accurate responses. We've also introduced a new endpoint, /api/ask, which enables users to interact with the AI directly from their browser.

On the development front, we've made several commits to our codebase. In acreetionos-immutable, we've updated the release.yml file to fix a validation issue. We've also re-triggered the GitLab mirror to ensure our code is up-to-date. In AcreetionOS-Xlibre, we've added the firefox-ublock-origin package to our build process. Finally, we've made some minor adjustments to our scripts to ensure they comply with shellcheck standards.

We're proud to say that our community is growing, and we're grateful for the contributions from our users. If you're interested in getting involved, we encourage you to join our Discord server or reach out to us directly. Your input and feedback are invaluable in shaping the future of AcreetionOS.

As always, we're committed to providing a secure and user-friendly experience for our users. We're constantly working to improve our distribution and address any issues that may arise. If you have any concerns or suggestions, please don't hesitate to reach out.

In other news, our co-lead developer, Darren Clift, has been busy working on various projects, including Calamares customization and ISO builds. He's also been exploring Cloudflare and backend development. Natalie Spiva, our other co-lead developer, has been focusing on the frontend and has been working on several projects, including Fluorite Browser and Cryolite Browser.

We're excited to see the progress being made on these projects and look forward to sharing more updates with you in the future. In the meantime, we encourage you to stay up-to-date with the latest developments by following us on social media or joining our community channels.

Thank you for your continued support, and we look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift

Co-Lead Developers, AcreetionOS
